items.act: check for obstructions, engineering and refueling activity
items.d:
[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-03-A-00010458.0001001 · GENERAL:]
Safety exterior inspections ensure that the aircraft and the external environment of the aircraft are safe for operation. When the flight crew arrives at the aircraft, they must check for, or be informed of any obstructions near the aircraft, engineering activity, or refueling activity, etc.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-03-A-00010461.0001001 · WHEEL CHOCKS:]
• WHEEL CHOCKS...... CHECK CM2-CM3
If the wheel chocks are not in position, the flight crew must check that the parking brake is set with sufficient accumulator pressure.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-03-A-00010462.0001001 · LANDING GEAR DOORS:]
• LANDING GEAR DOORS......CHECK POSITION CM2-CM3
WARNING If any landing gear door is open, do not pressurize the hydraulic systems until clearance is obtained from ground personnel.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-03-A-00010463.0001001 · APU AREA:]
• APU AREA...... CHECK CM2-CM3
Observe that the APU inlet and outlet are clear.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-A-00010897.0001001 · ENG:]
• ENG 1, 2 MASTERS LEVERS......OFF CM2

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-A-00011881.0009001 · WEATHER RADAR:]
• * WXR/PWS sw......OFF CM2

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-A-00010898.0001001 · L/G:]
• L/G lever...... DOWN CM2

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-A-00010899.0001001 · WIPERS:]
• Both WIPER selectors......OFF CM2

items.item: BAT 1 pb-sw, BAT 2 pb-sw and APU BAT pb-sw
items.d:
[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00010900.0002001:]
• BAT 1 pb-sw, BAT 2 pb-sw and APU BAT pb-sw......AUTO CM2
[Card vs FCOM:] the quick reference card prints 'ELEC, Bat ON'; the FCOM step is the line quoted above.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-C-00025222.0001001 · RMP:]
• RMP 1 and 2...... CHECK ON CM2

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-C-00010902.0001001 · APU FIRE:]
• APU FIRE TEST pb ......PRESS and MAINTAIN CM2
Check that the APU fire detection and extinguishing system is operative:
‐ APU FIRE warning on (if AC power available):
‐ ECAM
‐ CRC
‐ MASTER WARN light.
‐ APU FIRE pb-sw lighted red (lighted partially if AC power not available)
‐ SQUIB light and DISCH light on.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-C-00010903.0002001 · APU START:]
• APU START pb-sw...... ON CM2
Note: In cold weather conditions (below approximately 10 °C), the flight crew may observe a bleed pressure up to 12 PSI with possible fluctuations on the APU SD page and the BLEED SD page.
For more information on APU starter limitations and APU operations during refueling:
‐ Refer to LIM-APU APU Start
‐ Refer to LIM-APU APU Start/Shutdown during Refueling/Defueling.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-C-00010903.0002001 · APU START:]
• APU BLEED pb-sw...... ON CM2
Do not use APU BLEED, if the ground personnel confirms that a LP or HP ground air unit is connected to the aircraft. To determine if a HP ground air unit is connected, the flight crew should also check on the BLEED SD page, if there is pressure in the bleed air system.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00011860.0004001 · ADIRS:]
• * ALL IR MODE selector......NAV CM2
Align or realign IRS as appropriate. Refer to FCTM/PR-NP-SOP-40 ADIRS Operations. A complete IRS alignment must be performed in the following cases:
‐ Before the first flight of the day, or
‐ When there is a crew change, or
‐ When the departure airport is located between latitudes 2 ° north and 2 ° south, or
‐ When the GPS is not available and the NAVAID coverage is poor on the expected route, or
‐ When the GPS is not available and the expected flight time is more than 3 h. A fast IRS alignment must be performed if a complete IRS alignment is not necessary. To perform an alignment, the aircraft must be stopped on ground. Do not align IRS during engine start, or while the engines are running. In the case of aircraft movement during the IRS alignment, the flight crew must perform a new full alignment.
[Card vs FCOM:] the quick reference card prints 'ADIRS ON'; the FCOM step is the line quoted above.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00010908.0001001 · COCKPIT LIGHTS:]
• * COCKPIT LIGHTS...... AS RQRD CM1-CM2
Set INT LT, FLOOD LT, INTEG LT (included glareshield and FCU).

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00010908.0001001 · COCKPIT LIGHTS:]
• * COCKPIT LIGHTS...... AS RQRD CM1-CM2
Set INT LT, FLOOD LT, INTEG LT (included glareshield and FCU).

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-90000080.9000329 · CHECK THE MCDU:]
• MCDU...... ON CM1
Short press of the BRT button will switch ON the MCDU, if it is OFF. Use the brightness buttons (BRT and DIM) to adjust the brightness as required.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021766.0001001 · EFB START:]
• ALL EFB......START ALL

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021759.0002001:]
• * RCL pb...... PRESS 3 s CM1
This action recalls all the warnings that the flight crew cleared or cancelled during the last flight.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021759.0002001:]
• * AIRCRAFT ACCEPTANCE......PERFORM CM1
Note: The aircraft acceptance can be performed later, but must be completed at the end of the Cockpit Preparation.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021759.0002001:]
• * LOGBOOK AND MEL/CDL ITEMS......CHECK ALL
‐ Check the deferred items list
‐ Crosscheck with ECAM recall. All flight crewmembers:
‐ Check and discuss the technical condition of the aircraft (deferred items list)
‐ Check and discuss the MEL items (including the associated operational procedures, if any) and the CDL items. This includes the acceptability of the MEL and CDL items and the influence on the flight plan
‐ In icing conditions with OAT at or below +1 °C (34 °F), check the taxi-in time in freezing fog of the previous flight recorded in the logbook. This time will be used to determine the remaining taxi-out time before the next engine acceleration for ice shedding (Refer to PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR Engine Ice Shedding on Ground ).

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021760.0001001:]
• * JEPPESEN CHARTS...... PREPARE ALL
Prepare the necessary charts for the flight. Ensure the flight plan routing and ETPs are input in the
Jeppesen FD Pro application.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021760.0001001:]
• * ATIS...... OBTAIN CM2-CM3
The CM2 (CM3) should attain the ATIS. Obtain data needed for initializing the system, preparing the cockpit and for preliminary takeoff performance computation. The airfield data should include: RUNWAY IN USE, ALTIMETER SETTING, and WEATHER DATA.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021760.0001001:]
• * JEPPESEN CHARTS...... PREPARE ALL
Prepare the necessary charts for the flight. Ensure the flight plan routing and ETPs are input in the
Jeppesen FD Pro application.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021760.0001001:]
• * ACARS...... INITIALIZE PF
Initialize and check the ACARS. On the ACARS INIT page input/check the departure airport,
destination airport, flight number and date.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-00021760.0001001:]
• * PRELIMINARY TAKEOFF PERF DATA...... OBTAIN PF
From the AeroData TPR (or TLR) the PF reviews the following:
‐ RWY to be used
‐ RWY intersection
‐ Flaps setting
‐ Use of anti-ice
‐ Use of packs
‐ Takeoff thrust setting options (FLEX, TOGA).

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00021790.0002001 · ECAM PAGES - PAX:]
• * OXY......CHECK PRESSURE PM

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010909.0001001 · F/CTL:]
• FLAPS......CHECK POSITION PM
Check the upper ECAM display to confirm that the FLAPS position agrees with the handle position.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010909.0001001 · F/CTL:]
• * SPEED BRAKE lever...... CHECK RETRACTED and DISARMED PM
WARNING If flight control surface positions do not agree with the control handle positions, check with the maintenance crew before applying hydraulic power.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010910.0001001 · PARKING BRAKE:]
• * ACCU PRESS indicator...... CHECK PM
The ACCU PRESS indication must be in the green band. If required use the electric pump on blue hydraulic system to recharge the brake accumulator.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010910.0001001 · PARKING BRAKE:]
• * PARK BRK handle...... ON PM
When one brake temperature is above 500 °C (or above 350 °C with the brake fans  ON), avoid applying the parking brake, unless operationally necessary.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010910.0001001 · PARKING BRAKE:]
• * BRAKES PRESS indicator......CHECK PM
Check for normal indications.
WARNING The blue electric pump pressurizes the blue hydraulic system. If 'Maintenance in Progress' placard is displayed, get ground crew clearance before energizing the electric pump. In the absence of the placard, flight crew may energize the electric pump without notifying the ground crew.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010911.0001001 · ALTERNATE BRAKING SYSTEM:]
• CHOCKS...... CHECK IN PLACE PM

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010919.0001001 · EMERGENCY EQUIPMENT:]
• EMER EQPT...... CHECK PM-CM3
Check that:
‐ Life vests are stowed
‐ Crash axe is stowed
‐ Smoke hoods  and/or portable oxygen equipment and full-face masks  is stowed and ready for use
‐ Portable fire extinguisher is lockwired and the pressure gauge indicator is in the green area
‐ Oxygen masks are stowed
‐ Flashlights are stowed
‐ Escape ropes are stowed
‐ PED Fire Containment Bag is stowed
‐ Fire gloves are stowed

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010920.0001001:]
• RAIN RPLNT indicators...... CHECK PRESSURE and QUANTITY PM-CM3
CAUTION Never use rain repellent to wash the windshield and never use it on a dry windshield.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-04-D-00010921.0002001 · LANDING GEAR PINS:]
• * GEAR PINS...... CHECK ONBOARD and STOWED PM-CM3
Check that the three gear pins are onboard and stowed.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-A-00011857.0001001 · WHITE LIGHTS ON THE OVERHEAD PANEL:]
• * ALL WHITE LIGHTS...... OFF PF
Note:
‐ Check with maintenance if a light is left illuminated on the maintenance panel.
‐ During the scan of the overhead panel, check also that the only amber lights are the GEN FAULT lights.
[Exterior lights, quick reference (technique):] PF: Strobes AUTO · Nav 1 · All others OFF

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-05-A-00011096.0001001 · SCHEMATIC:]
Refer to PRO-NOR-SOP-05 Exterior Walkaround

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-B-00011875.0001001 · ISIS:]
• * ISIS...... CHECK PF
‐ Adjust brightness.
‐ Check IAS, altimeter readings, altimeter settings and attitude display.
‐ Check no flags - Reset attitude, if necessary. Note: Use of ISIS bugs function is not recommended (Refer to DSC-34-10-20 ISIS).

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-C-00011889.0001001 · RMP:]
• RMP 1 and 2 ......CHECK ON PF

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-D-90000090.9000245 · INIT A PAGE (PART 2):]
• TO/FROM...... CHECK PF
Press the INIT button on the MCDU to display the INIT A page. Check the TO/FROM field [1R] to confirm the correct flight plan uplink occurred. If the TO/FROM field is incorrect, the flight plan can be deleted by cycling the FMS NAV Database (Refer to PRO-NOR-SOP-04 DATA page).

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-D-00015238.0001001:]
• * FMS PREPARATION...... CROSSCHECK PM
After the PF prepares the FMS, the PM checks all the data entered in the FMS. This check includes a crosscheck between:
‐ Waypoints of the expected departure route that include constraints
‐ Waypoints of the flight plan and the computerized flight plan
‐ Initial cruise altitude and the computerized flight plan
‐ Total track miles and the computerized flight plan
‐ Fuel remaining at destination and the computerized flight plan
‐ Performance data including modifications of the THR RED/ACCEL/EO ACCEL settings, if applicable
‐ TRANS ALT in the ACTIVE/PERF page
‐ Setup of the SEC flight plan. The PM should have the same mental image of the intended departure procedure, trajectory, and constraints as the PF. The PM should check with the PF if anything is not clear. For more information, Refer to FCTM/PR-NP-SOP-60 Check of Departure Preparation.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-E-00020728.0001001 · EFIS CONTROL PANEL:]
• * BAROMETRIC REFERENCE......SET/CROSSCHECK BOTH
‐ Set QNH on the EFIS control panel and on the standby altimeter
‐ Check the barometric reference and altitude indications on the PFDs and on the standby altimeter. The maximum difference is: ±20 ft between both PFDs ±60 ft between ISIS and PFDs, 75 ft between PFDs and airport elevation (Refer to PRO-SPO-50 RVSM for more information).

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-00011910.0001001:]
• OXYGEN MASK TEST...... PERFORM PF-PM
For a detailed test of the mask, Refer to DSC-35-20-30 How to Test the Mask.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-00011911.0002001:]
• * PFD......CHECK PF-PM
‐ Check PFD/ND not transferred
‐ Check for correct display, when ATT and HDG are available
‐ Check IAS, FMA, initial target ALT, altimeter readings, VSI, altimeter settings, heading and attitude display.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-00011885.0001001 · ECAM CONTROL PANEL:]
• * PRESS pb......PRESS PF
Check that the CAB PRESS SD page displays LDG ELEV AUTO to confirm correct position of the LDG ELEV knob.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-00011912.0001001:]
• * IRS ALIGN......CHECK PM
On the POSITION MONITOR page, check that the IRS are in NAV mode, and check that the distance between each IRS and the FMS position is lower than 5 NM. Select ND in ROSE-NAV or ARC mode, and confirm that the aircraft position is consistent with the position of the airport, the SID and the surrounding NAVAIDs.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-90000100.9000254:]
• RELEASE VERSION #__/ FITNESS/ FOB/ PDSC...... SENT PF
Electronically accept latest flight release version fitness for duty, Fuel on Board and PDSC time via OPS CTRL MSG page in ACARS.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-00024946.0001001:]
• * FUEL ON BOARD......CHECK PF-PM
‐ Check that ECAM FOB corresponds to the block fuel of the computerized flight plan
‐ On FUEL SD page, check that the fuel is correctly balanced and CG is within operational limits.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-90000101.9000253 · ATC CLEARANCE:]
• ATC clearance...... CONFIRM PM
Obtain ATC clearance via VHF, ACARS (PDC) or via CPDLC (DCL), Refer to PRO-SUP-46 Departure Clearance via CPDLC.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-90000102.9000255:]
• DEPARTURE LEGS VERIFICATION...... PERFORM BOTH
The PF reads from the “glass” (ND), and the PM verifies against the “paper” (Flight Plan/ Navigation Log, Jeppesen Charts and ATC Clearance).
‐ Select PLAN mode on EFIS Control Panel.
‐ Select CSTR pb ON, on EFIS Control Panel, to display speed/altitude constraints.
‐ Select F-PLN on MCDU.
‐ Read aloud each Departure and Enroute waypoint and corresponding speed/altitude constraint (if any) off the ND.
‐ After each waypoint, select the ‘UP’ arrow key on the MCDU to display the next waypoint.
‐ Check all “non-defined” waypoints (waypoints that are not in Jeppesen FD Pro Charts or the FMS database, or waypoints in an expired Nav database) and all “user-defined” waypoints (waypoints entered via LAT/LONG inputs). This check is achieved by doing the following: • Select the left LSK next to the non-defined waypoint to display the LAT REV page. • Read aloud the full Latitude and Longitude located at the top of the LAT REV page. • Select the left LSK next to < RETURN. …
‐ Follow along with the PF by checking each waypoint and constraint against the Jeppesen SID, Dispatch release, and current ATC clearance.
‐ Resolve any discrepancy.
The final step is to confirm that the total F-PLN distance (DIST) and the Estimated Fuel On Board (EFOB) at the destination agree with the Dispatch Release. Resolve any large discrepancies.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-06-00011915.0001001:]
• * DEPARTURE BRIEFING...... PERFORM BOTH
Perform a Threat Based Departure Briefing. For more information, refer to FOM "Threat Based Departure Briefing/ TPC".
[FCTM PR-NP-CL-00024935.0001001 · COCKPIT PREPARATION:]
Checklist trigger: Departure briefing completed.
✅ COCKPIT PREPARATION CHECKLIST: PF requests it, PM reads the challenge, PF responds after checking the aircraft. Card trigger: Departure Briefing complete. (FCTM PR-NP-CL-00024935.0001001)

items.d:
[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00021319.9000330 · LOAD CLOSEOUT - PASSENGER AIRCRAFT:]
• ACARS PERF page...... SELECT “*LOAD FMC” PF
The PF selects the “*LOAD FMC” prompt when it appears. This will allow the FMS to upload the ACARS final weight data and takeoff performance. Note: The first indication the final weight and takeoff performance data was transmitted to the aircraft (“*LOAD FMC” prompt available for selection) is usually when the ACARS printer begins to automatically print the Load closeout.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00021319.9000330 · LOAD CLOSEOUT - PASSENGER AIRCRAFT:]
• LOAD CLOSEOUT (LCO)......CHECK PF-PM
Both crew members carefully check the Load Closeout data is correct:
‐ Flight number / date
‐ Aircraft
‐ Crew Count
‐ Takeoff Fuel (“TOF”)
‐ Takeoff Weight (“TOW”) - crosscheck against the planned takeoff weight on the dispatch flight plan to determine if an adjustment to the MIN RLS FUEL and MIN TAKEOFF FUEL is required. For more information, refer to FOM “Flight Plan Weight Tolerances”
‐ Total persons on board (“TOB”)
‐ Jumpseat occupants
‐ ZFW/ZFWCG (“FMS ZFW/ZFCG”)
‐ Dangerous Goods (“NOTOC”)
‐ Animals (“AVI”)
‐ Federal Air Marshals (“FAM”)

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00021319.9000330 · LOAD CLOSEOUT - PASSENGER AIRCRAFT:]
• LOAD CLOSEOUT (LCO)......CHECK PF-PM
Both crew members carefully check the Load Closeout data is correct:
‐ Flight number / date
‐ Aircraft
‐ Crew Count
‐ Takeoff Fuel (“TOF”)
‐ Takeoff Weight (“TOW”) - crosscheck against the planned takeoff weight on the dispatch flight plan to determine if an adjustment to the MIN RLS FUEL and MIN TAKEOFF FUEL is required. For more information, refer to FOM “Flight Plan Weight Tolerances”
‐ Total persons on board (“TOB”)
‐ Jumpseat occupants
‐ ZFW/ZFWCG (“FMS ZFW/ZFCG”)
‐ Dangerous Goods (“NOTOC”)
‐ Animals (“AVI”)
‐ Federal Air Marshals (“FAM”)

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00011914.0001001 · FUEL:]
• MIN RLS FUEL...... CHECK PF-PM
Check that ECAM FOB is above Minimum Release Fuel on the flight plan.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00021320.0001001 · TAKEOFF DATA:]
• TAKEOFF PERFORMANCE......UPLINK FLX or UPLINK TOGA PF
The PF uplinks the Takeoff Data into the FMS PERF TO page. The crew can select to uplink either FLX or TOGA takeoff data. Note: When FLX takeoff performance data is uplinked to the FMS, behind the scenes TOGA takeoff data is also uplinked in case the flight crew chooses to revert to a TOGA thrust takeoff at a later time.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00021320.0001001 · TAKEOFF DATA:]
• FINAL TAKEOFF DATA (TPR/TLR)...... CHECK PF-PM
Both crew members carefully check the Final Takeoff Performance Report (TPR/TLR) data is correct:
‐ Aircraft / Flight number / date
‐ Wind / OAT / QNH
‐ Confirm it is the “FINAL” TPR (If using the TLR, confirm the TLR is still valid)
‐ Remarks
‐ Takeoff Runway / Intersection
‐ Engine Out Departure Procedure
‐ Air Conditioning on/off
‐ V speeds
‐ Flap Config/THS
‐ Flex / TOGA
‐ Compare the GTOW versus MTOW

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00021320.0001001 · TAKEOFF DATA:]
• FINAL TAKEOFF DATA (TPR/TLR)...... CHECK PF-PM
Both crew members carefully check the Final Takeoff Performance Report (TPR/TLR) data is correct:
‐ Aircraft / Flight number / date
‐ Wind / OAT / QNH
‐ Confirm it is the “FINAL” TPR (If using the TLR, confirm the TLR is still valid)
‐ Remarks
‐ Takeoff Runway / Intersection
‐ Engine Out Departure Procedure
‐ Air Conditioning on/off
‐ V speeds
‐ Flap Config/THS
‐ Flex / TOGA
‐ Compare the GTOW versus MTOW

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00011059.0001001 · MCDU:]
• FMS PERF TO page...... SELECT PF
It is recommended to display the PERF TAKEOFF page on the PF side.

items.item: SEATS, SEAT BELTS, HARNESSES, RUDDER PEDALS, ARMRESTS
items.d:
[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-A-00011058.0001001 · SEATING POSITION:]
• SEATS, SEAT BELTS, HARNESSES, RUDDER PEDALS, ARMRESTS...... PF-PM ...... ADJUST
The seat is correctly adjusted when the flight crew’s eyes are aligned with the red and white balls.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00011040.0004001 · PUSHBACK/START CLEARANCE:]
• PUSHBACK/START CLEARANCE...... OBTAIN PM
Obtain ATC pushback/start clearance and ground crew clearance.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00011064.0001001 · EXTERIOR LIGHTS:]
• BEACON sw...... ON PF
When cleared for start or pushback, set the BEACON sw to ON.
[Exterior lights, quick reference (technique):] PF: Beacon ON

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00015355.0001001 · ATC:]
• ATC......SET FOR OPERATION PM
ATC is set in accordance with airport requirements.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00011063.0002001 · WINDOWS AND DOORS:]
• WINDOWS and DOORS......CHECK CLOSED PF-PM
‐ To ensure that the sliding window is correctly closed and locked, push the handle of the sliding window fully forward to the closed position, and verify that the red indicator is no longer visible
‐ Check, on the ECAM lower display, that all the aircraft doors are closed
‐ When required by FOM policies, check that the cockpit door is closed and locked (no cockpit door open/fault indication). If entry is requested, identify the person requesting entry before unlocking the door. With the cockpit door selector on NORM, the cockpit door is closed and locked. If entry is requested from the cabin, and if no further action is performed by the pilot, the cabin crew will be able to unlock the door by using the emergency access procedure. …
Note: Starting one engine with a door not closed will result in pack valve closure.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00011063.0002001 · WINDOWS AND DOORS:]
• WINDOWS and DOORS......CHECK CLOSED PF-PM
‐ To ensure that the sliding window is correctly closed and locked, push the handle of the sliding window fully forward to the closed position, and verify that the red indicator is no longer visible
‐ Check, on the ECAM lower display, that all the aircraft doors are closed
‐ When required by FOM policies, check that the cockpit door is closed and locked (no cockpit door open/fault indication). If entry is requested, identify the person requesting entry before unlocking the door. With the cockpit door selector on NORM, the cockpit door is closed and locked. If entry is requested from the cabin, and if no further action is performed by the pilot, the cabin crew will be able to unlock the door by using the emergency access procedure. …
Note: Starting one engine with a door not closed will result in pack valve closure.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00011063.0002001 · WINDOWS AND DOORS:]
• SLIDES......CHECK ARMED PF-PM
Check, on the ECAM lower display, that all slides are armed.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00011063.0002001 · WINDOWS AND DOORS:]
• SLIDES......CHECK ARMED PF-PM
Check, on the ECAM lower display, that all slides are armed.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00011065.0001001 · THRUST LEVERS:]
• THRUST LEVERS ......IDLE PF
CAUTION The engines start regardless of the thrust lever position. If the thrust levers are not set to IDLE, then thrust rapidly increases to the corresponding thrust lever position, causing a hazardous situation.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-07-B-00011066.0002001 · PARKING BRAKE AND NOSEWHEEL STEERING:]
• PARK BRK handle ...... ON PF
When one brake temperature is above 300 °C , avoid applying the parking brake, unless operationally necessary.
[FCTM PR-NP-CL-00024936.0001001 · BEFORE START:]
Checklist trigger:
‐ Pushback clearance or start clearance received, and
‐ Before Start flow pattern completed.
✅ BEFORE START CHECKLIST: PF requests it, PM reads the challenge, PF responds after checking the aircraft. Card trigger: Before Start flow complete. (FCTM PR-NP-CL-00024936.0001001)

items.d:
[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011043.0004001 · ENG START SELECTOR:]
• ENG START selector......NORM PF
For additional information on the automatic starting sequence, Refer to DSC-70-80-30 Sequence of the Automatic Start.
After start, to avoid thermal shock, the engine must be operated at idle, or near idle for at least 5 min when engines are cold (3 min when engines are warm after a stop of 1.5 h or less) before advancing the thrust lever to high power. Taxi time at idle may be included in the warm-up period.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011048.0001001 · GROUND SPOILERS:]
• GND SPLRS...... ARM PM

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011044.0001001 · APU BLEED:]
• APU BLEED pb-sw......OFF PF
This action enables to avoid ingestion of engine exhaust gases.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011049.0001001 · RUDDER TRIM:]
• RUD TRIM RESET pb......PRESS PM
Press the RESET pb on the RUD TRIM panel.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011045.0003001 · ANTI-ICE:]
• ENG 1 and 2 ANTI-ICE pb-sw......AS RQRD PF
Engine anti-ice must be set to ON during all ground operations, when icing conditions exist or are anticipated.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011050.0001001 · FLAPS:]
• FLAPS lever...... SET FOR TAKEOFF PM

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011047.0001001 · APU:]
• APU MASTER SW pb-sw...... OFF PF

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011051.0003001 · PITCH TRIM:]
• PITCH TRIM wheel...... CHECK PM
Check the takeoff CG on the PITCH TRIM wheel using the CG indication on the ECAM.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011054.0001001 · ECAM STATUS:]
• ECAM STATUS......CHECK BOTH
The PM checks and the PF crosschecks that there is no status reminder (STS) on the E/WD
If STS appears on the E/WD, press the STS pb to display the STATUS page.

[FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-09-A-00011054.0001001 · ECAM STATUS:]
• ECAM STATUS......CHECK BOTH
The PM checks and the PF crosschecks that there is no status reminder (STS) on the E/WD
If STS appears on the E/WD, press the STS pb to display the STATUS page.

Note: The flight crew must operate the engines at or near idle thrust for a cooling period of 1 min before engine shutdown, in order to thermally stabilize the engines. Idle reverse thrust and normal thrust to maneuver during taxi (i.e. at or near idle), are not considered as high thrust operations. Therefore, both of the following applies:
‐ If the flight crew used idle reverse thrust for landing and normal thrust to maneuver during taxi after landing, the cooling period starts when the flight crew retards the thrust lever during the flare
‐ If the flight crew used maximum reverse for landing, the cooling period starts when the flight crew sets the thrust lever to idle reverse during the landing rollout. Before engine shutdown, routine cooling periods that last less than the required time, can result in engine degradation.

PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR.title: FCOM PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR - Engine Ice Shedding on Ground
PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR.body:
CAUTION During engine operations on ground in icing conditions, and with the OAT at or below 1 °C (34 °F), ice accretion may affect the fan and core engine parts. Apply the following procedure for engine ice shedding to prevent possible engine degradation or damage. The quantity of ice accretion depends on the time during which the engine is running on ground in the above-mentioned icing conditions.
This procedure involves the performance of engine accelerations before the end of specific time intervals. The taxi-out time starts when the first engine is running, and finishes when the aircraft is aligned on the departure runway for takeoff. The taxi-in time starts at touchdown, and finishes when both engines are set to off. The flight crew can check the following diagram to anticipate the procedure to be performed during taxi-out. …

PRO-NOR-SUP-SEC.title: FCOM PRO-NOR-SUP-SEC - Securing the Aircraft
PRO-NOR-SUP-SEC.body:
The flight crew should apply the following procedure, when the last additional aircraft occupant left the aircraft and the securing of the aircraft is intended. Airbus recommends performing the following procedure when the aircraft is left unattended: i.e. no qualified flight crew or ground crew are in the cockpit to supervise and monitor the aircraft systems. Prior to performing this check, the following SUP Adverse Weather procedures should be taken into account when appropriate: ‐ Securing the aircraft for cold soak (Refer to PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR Securing the Aircraft for Cold Soak). ‐ Water system draining (Refer to PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR Water System Depressurization or Draining - General). ‐ Operations on contaminated airports (Refer to PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR Parking). ‐ Operations with volcanic ash, sand or dust (Refer to PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR Securing the Aircraft).
